the study of protein-protein interactions, where we developed a new coarse-grained model for the electrostatic and the accessible surface area contributions, and applied it to the study of protein association.
the construction of a coarse-graining model for proteins that is able to capture the main physical properties of the protein-solvent system.
the study of protein-protein interaction using a coarse-grained model specifically designed for proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present coarse-grained approach provides a good approximation to all-atom potentials of mean force when the distance between molecules is large enough for the solvent to be considered as a continuous dielectric, and it can be improved at short distances by an all-atom refinement.

the coarse-graining of the protein accessible surface area and the electrostatics of proteins is a good approximation of all-atoms calculations, but that the description of short range interactions, like the ones found in the SOD dimer, requires a refinement of the electrostatic model.

the coarse-graining procedure is able to provide a reasonable approximation to the potential of mean interaction between proteins and peptides, with the exception of the electrostatic desolavtion contribution for very short distance interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our coarse-grained potential provides a very good description for the interaction between proteins, which is in good agreement with the all-atoms results, while the computational cost of our model is significantly lower than the one of the full all-atoms approach.

the coarse-graining of the protein surface area, as well as the coarse-graining and implicit solvent treatment of the electrostatics, is an effective and computationally efficient way of modeling protein-protein interactions.
the coarse-graining approach provides a good approximation to all-atom simulations for the electrostatic contribution to the protein-protein association free-energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
coarse-grained models, like the one we have presented here, can be used to study the association of proteins and peptides, provided that the range of the interactions is not too short.
coarse-grained models of the type we have developed can be successfully used to study the interaction of proteins with a reasonable accuracy.
the coarse-graining of the solvent-accessible surface of proteins and peptides provides an efficient and accurate representation for the study of protein-protein interactions.
